div.head: ECf 35.1a
div.ab: — Cui Cristine rex Eadwardus dedit terram quam habuit postea Radulfus de Limisei —.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 665 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

note.seg: 35, 1a muss, da quem in 35, 1b den Aetheling meint, Parenthese sein und bezeugt, weil ohne Zusammenhang mit Leges oder dem Bekenner, des Verfs. Interesse für diese terram oder Limézy. Christine erhielt alle oder die meisten Güter (nicht 1058—65, wie Verf. meint) von Wilhelm I. und starb 1095—1100. Ihre Güter erhielt Limézy 1086—93. Sie liegen (ausser Bradwell, Oxfordshire) in Warwickshire, und dorthin, nach Coventry, verlegte Bischof Robert von Limézy 1102 seine Kathedrale. Rudolf starb nach 1114 und vor 1131. Vgl. mein Über Edw. Conf. 10 ff. 21; dazu Round Hist. of Hamps. I 410; Cal. of doc. in France I n. 1278, wo eine von Rudolf bezeugte Urkunde a. 1102—28 steht

35, 1a must be a parenthesis, since quem in 35, 1b means the Ætheling; and, having no connection with the Leges or the Confessor, it attests the author’s interest in this terram or in Limésy. Christine received all or most of her estates (not 1058–65, as the author thinks) from William I and died 1095–1100. Her estates went to Limésy 1086–93. They lie (except Bradwell, Oxfordshire) in Warwickshire, and it was there, to Coventry, that Bishop Robert of Limésy moved his cathedral in 1102. Rudolf died after 1114 and before 1131. Cf. my Über Edw. Conf. 10 ff. 21; also Round, Hist. of Hamps. I 410; Cal. of doc. in France I no. 1278, where there is a charter of 1102–28 witnessed by Rudolf
